summary: Overview of Saudi Arabia, a state formed from four regions (Hejaz, Najd, Al-Ahsa and 'Asir) and founded in 1932 by Ibn Saud after conquests that began with Riyadh in 1902. It is an absolute monarchy shaped by Wahhabi Sunni Islam and home to Islam's two holiest sites. The note also gives population figures and the official language.
one_line: Saudi Arabia is an absolute monarchy founded in 1932 by Ibn Saud, shaped by Wahhabism and home to Mecca and Medina.
key_facts: The area of modern-day Saudi Arabia formerly consisted of four distinct regions: Hejaz, Najd, parts of Eastern Arabia (Al-Ahsa) and Southern Arabia ('Asir).
The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia was founded in 1932 by Ibn Saud.
Ibn Saud united the four regions into a single state through a series of conquests beginning in 1902 with the capture of Riyadh.
Riyadh was the ancestral home of the House of Saud, Ibn Saud's family.
Saudi Arabia has been an absolute monarchy, effectively a hereditary dictatorship governed along Islamic lines.
The ultraconservative Wahhabi movement within Sunni Islam has been called "the predominant feature of Saudi culture".
The global spread of Wahhabism has been largely financed by the oil and gas trade.
Saudi Arabia is sometimes called "the Land of the Two Holy Mosques", referring to Al-Masjid al-Haram in Mecca and Al-Masjid an-Nabawi in Medina.
As of 2013, Saudi Arabia's population was 28.7 million, including 20 million Saudi nationals and 8 million foreigners.
As of 2017, the population of Saudi Arabia is 33 million.
The official language of Saudi Arabia is Arabic.
